sentences.text: BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE ASHISH SHROTI  ON THE 9 th OF MAY, 2025
MISC. APPEAL No. 1070 of 2007
NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY HAVING  Versus  DILIP SINGH AND OTHERS  Appearance:

entities.text: NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY HAVING  Versus  DILIP SINGH AND OTHERS
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Mr. Shriniwas Gajendragadkar - Advocate for the appellan  Company.
Ms. Meena Singhal - Advocate for the respondents.

ORDER The appellant - Insurance Company has filed this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 challenging the award dated 26.07.2007 passed by 4th Additional Motor Accident, Claims Tribunal, Morena, in Claim Case No.63/2007, wherein the liability to pay compensation has been fastened on the appellant - Insurance Company.
2 . The findings which are not under challenged in this appeal are that the claimant - Phool Singh suffered certain injuries in the accident occurred on 07.04.2016 with Commander Jeep No.MP07-H-6939.

entities.text: 4th Additional Motor Accident, Claims Tribunal, Morena
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
He lodged a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988,
claiming compensation on account of the injuries suffered by him.

The Claims Tribunal has passed the impugned award directing the Insurance Company to pay an amount of Rs.25,000/- towards NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:10290 2 MA-1070-2007 compensation along with interest @ 7% per annum.
The appeal has been filed by the Insurance Company challenging the findings of the Claims Tribunal, wherein the Insurance Company has been held liable to pay the compensation.
The first ground of challenge is that the offending vehicle was insured as private vehicle but was being used as passenger vehicle at the time of accident.
The second ground of challenge is that the maximum capacity of the offending vehicle was 9 passengers, whereas, at the time of accident, there were 14-15 persons traveling therein.
The third ground of challenge is that the insurance policy was "Act only Policy", which would not cover the passengers traveling in the offending vehicle.

National Insurance Company Having vs Dilip Singh on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31621879/
1 3 .

entities.text: National Insurance Company Having vs Dilip Singh on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the other hand, the learned counsel appearing for respondent/claimant vehemently opposed the submissions made by appellant's counsel.
She submitted that there is no evidence available on record to show that the respondent was travelling as a paid passenger.
She also submitted that there is nothing on record to establish that there were 14-15 passengers travelling in offending vehicle.

She further submitted that the Insurance Company has taken premium of Rs.450/- for all 9 passengers which is evident from the policy document and, therefore, it cannot be said that it was an Act only Policy.
She thus prays for dismissal of appeal.

4 . Considered the arguments of both the sides and perused the record.
5 .

So far as first ground of challenge is concerned, the learned NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:10290 3 MA-1070-2007 counsel for the appellant - Insurance Company submitted that the claimant - Phool Singh was not the relative of the owner/driver of the vehicle,
therefore, there is a presumption that he was travelling in offending vehicle as a paid passenger.
In this regard, the claimant Phool Singh has stated in para-8 in his evidence that the driver of the vehicle was known to him.
When a specific question was put to him, he denied that he paid anything to driver for travelling in vehicle.

Therefore, the fact that claimant was not the relative of driver/owner of vehicle becomes insignificant and the fact that claimant was known to driver of the vehicle and was, therefore, permitted to travel in vehicle, is sufficient to hold that he was not a paid passenger.
Therefore, the finding recorded by the Tribunal, that the claimant - Phool Singh was not a paid passenger cannot be said to be perverse and is accordingly upheld.
6. The learned counsel for the appellant then argued that there were 14-15 persons travelling in vehicle as against its maximum capacity of 9 passengers.

In this regard, except the FIR (Ex. P/2),
there is no iota of evidence on record in support of this contention.
On the contrary, claimant- Phool Singh, in para-7 of his evidence, has specifically denied that there were 14-15 persons traveling in the vehicle.
The finding in this regard could not have been recorded solely on the basis of FIR without there being any corroborating evidence.
This issue has been considered by Apex Court in the case of Halappa Vs. Malik Sab, reported in (2018)12 SCC 15.

entities.text: Halappa Vs. Malik Sab, reported in (2018)12 SCC 15
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Again in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:10290 4 MA-1070-2007 Chamundeswari and others, reported in (2021)18 SCC 596 the Apex Court held as under:
"8. It is clear from the evidence on record of PW 1 as well as PW 3 that the Eicher van which was going in front of the car, had taken a sudden right turn without giving any signal or indicator.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:10290 4 MA-1070-2007 Chamundeswari and others, reported in (2021)18 SCC 596
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The evidence of PW 1 & PW 3 is categorical and in absence of any rebuttal evidence by examining the driver of Eicher van, the High Court has rightly held that the accident occurred only due to the negligence of the driver of Eicher van.
It is to be noted that PW 1 herself travelled in the very car and PW 3, who has given statement before the police, was examined as eyewitness.
In view of such evidence on record, there is no reason to give weightage to the contents of the first information report.

If any evidence before the Tribunal runs contrary to the contents in the first information report, the evidence which is recorded before the Tribunal has to be given weightage over the contents of the first information report."

2 7 .

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, in absence of any corroborative evidence, the FIR alone cannot be relied upon to hold that there were 14-15 persons traveling in the vehicle.
The argument of appellant's counsel is thus not acceptable.

8 . The last contention of the learned counsel for the appellant company is that the "act upon policy"
would not cover the passengers traveling in the vehicle.

In this regard, if the policy document (Ex.
P-2) is seen, it is gathered that separate premium of Rs.450/- was taken by Insurance Company covering nine passengers.
Therefore, the Company cannot avoid its liability to cover those passengers.
Accordingly, this ground of appellant's counsel is also not acceptable and stands rejected.

9 . At this stage, counsel for the claimants submitted that even NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:10290 5 MA-1070-2007 though no cross-objection has been filed in this appeal,
this Court can consider the issue of enhancement of compensation by exercising power under Order 41 Rule 33 of CPC.

In this regard, she relied upon the Full Bench judgment of this Court in the case of Prakramchand Vs. Chhuttan and others, reported in 1991 JLJ 733 and Savitha Vs.
Cholamandalam MS General Ins.Co.Ltd. and others, reported in 2020 ACJ 2157 .

entities.text: Prakramchand Vs. Chhuttan and others, reported in 1991 JLJ 733
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
Savitha Vs.
Cholamandalam MS General Ins.Co.Ltd. and others, reported in 2020 ACJ 2157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
She also placed reliance upon Delhi High Court judgment in the case of Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Madhu Bala,
reported in 2020 ACJ 1025 (Delhi) .

entities.text:
Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Madhu Bala,
reported in 2020 ACJ 1025 (Delhi)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 0 . Considered the argument of counsel for respondent/claimant.
Admittedly respondent has not filed any cross-objection praying for enhancement of compensation.
The case of Savitha (supra) was an appeal of claimants only and, therefore, issue raised by respondent's counsel was not involved therein.

In the case of Madhu Bala before Delhi High Court also, even though the compensation was enhanced in the appeal of Insurance Company, however, the court has not laid down parameters in which such a power can be exercised.
This judgment also, therefore, does not help the respondent.
In the case of Chuttan (supra), the Full Bench of this Court held that the court can exercise powers under Order 41 Rule 33 CPC in order to do justice and arrive at just compensation.
However, such power should be exercised in rare cases in compelling circumstances.
If the facts of this case are seen, the accident took place on 07.04.2006.
Looking to the injuries suffered by respondent, the Tribunal awarded him compensation which was found adequate at that point of time.
The NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:10290 6 MA-1070-2007 respondent also felt satisfied and accepted the same and therefore, did not file appeal for enhancement.
Therefore, this court does not find this to be a fit case to exercise power under Order 41 Rule 33 CPC for enhancing compensation.
The argument of learned counsel for respondent is thus rejected.
11 . In view of the discussion made above, the appeal filed by appellant insurance company is found to be without any substance and is accordingly dismissed.

(ASHISH SHROTI) JUDGE bj/-
